title: Worrying is self-fulfilling: replace it with preparation
summary: Jason argues that worry actively causes the bad outcomes it fears, because it injects second-guessing and fear into the moment of execution. The antidote isn't apathy but preparation: long-term deliberate practice and short-term visualization, then clearing your mind and executing. He applies this to the many worries founders carry.

principles.text: Worry is a self-fulfilling prophecy; it breaks things that aren't broken instead of leading to solutions.
principles.quote: "Worry" causes the thing you're worried about, to actually happen.

principles.text: The opposite of worry is preparation, not apathy.
principles.quote: The opposite of "Worry" isn't "Apathy". The opposite is "Preparation".

principles.text: Prepare long-term: purposeful repetition of specific skills and planning effort across a season so you peak when it matters.
principles.quote: They plan energy output and practice-schedules across an entire season, such that they peak during the most important meets.

principles.text: Visualize the action ahead of time, then clear your mind and execute on muscle memory rather than thinking mid-action.
principles.quote: you should visualize the shot ahead of time, then clear your mind and execute using muscle-memory.

principles.text: Once you've done the practice, stop second-guessing; mistakes matter less than you think since nobody is counting but you.
principles.quote: you should realize you've already done all the practice required, and mistakes don't actually matter anyway. No one is counting except you.

principles.text: Founder worries (payroll, competitors, closing a customer, metrics) are destructive; tackle the root constructively, prepare, then proceed.
principles.quote: Instead, tackle the root of the worry constructively, prepare yourself as best you can, and then just proceed.
